verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits the specified commission or advisory body to process sensitive or criminal data where obtaining explicit consent is impossible or disproportionately burdensome. Provision B requires a controller to be able to demonstrate consent where processing is based on consent; superficially, A's dispensation from seeking consent could appear inconsistent with a consent-proof obligation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 7 GDPR applies only "Wanneer de verwerking berust op toestemming" (where processing is based on consent). Processing under A is instead justified by a task of substantial public interest and specified safeguards, precisely in circumstances where requesting explicit consent is impossible or disproportionate; it is therefore not processing based on consent and does not trigger B's demonstration requirement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het vragen van uitdrukkelijke toestemming onmogelijk blijkt of een onevenredige inspanning vergt
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de verwerking berust op toestemming, moet de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kunnen aantonen dat de betrokkene toestemming heeft gegeven voor de verwerking van zijn persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: De inhoud en eventuele verplichting van een mededeling aan een betrokkene over een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 11.3a A formuleert dat een kennisgeving aan de betrokkene ten minste de aard van de inbreuk, informatiebronnen en aanbevolen beperkende maatregelen omvat. Artikel 34 B bepaalt daarentegen dat een individuele mededeling aan de betrokkene onder drie omstandigheden niet vereist is, waaronder wanneer een openbare mededeling in de plaats komt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A legt uitsluitend inhoudelijke minimumeisen op voor het geval er een kennisgeving aan de betrokkene wordt gedaan; het zegt niet dat die kennisgeving in alle gevallen moet worden gedaan. B bepaalt wanneer die mededeling niet vereist is; in die gevallen ontstaat dus geen A-verplichting om de inhoud van een niet te verzenden kennisgeving op te nemen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene is niet vereist wanneer een van de volgende voorwaarden is vervuld:

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of sensitive/personal information in the context of services, including potentially public health-related online services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A public-law health-care institution may be subject to A's confidentiality duty when processing health data and to B when providing an information-society service. A consent-based design could conceivably be used to control access to confidential health information, whereas B prohibits conditioning access to the public body's service on consent referred to in paragraph 1.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts: A requires secrecy by persons processing health data, while B prohibits a public-law entity from making service access conditional on consent for storing or accessing information in a user's device. B does not require disclosure of health data, and A does not require obtaining or making access conditional on the device-information consent covered by B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is hij verplicht tot geheimhouding van de gegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: De toegang van de gebruiker tot een dienst van de informatiemaatschappij die wordt geleverd door of namens een krachtens publiekrecht ingestelde rechtspersoon wordt niet afhankelijk gemaakt van het verlenen van toestemming als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Administratieve verplichtingen rond gegevensverwerking en cybersecurityincidenten voor organisaties/entiteiten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit met minder dan 250 werknemers kan op grond van A zijn vrijgesteld van het bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten. Als een significant cyberincident persoonsgegevens betreft, kan het ontbreken van zo’n register de entiteit feitelijk bemoeilijken om de voor B vereiste incidentinformatie snel te verzamelen en te rapporteren.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A schept uitsluitend een uitzondering op de AVG-verplichting om een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten bij te houden; zij verbiedt geen verwerking, vastlegging of verstrekking van gegevens. B legt een afzonderlijke meldplicht op aan essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten bij significante incidenten. Een entiteit kan dus zowel onder de uitzondering van A vallen als volledig voldoen aan haar meldplicht uit B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben, tenzij het waarschijnlijk is dat de verwerking die zij verrichten een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkenen, de verwerking niet incidenteel is, of de verwerking bijzondere categorieën van gegevens, als bedoeld in artikel 9, lid 1, of persoonsgegevens in verband met strafrechtelijke veroordelingen en strafbare feiten als bedoeld in artikel 10 betreft.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: Verstrekking van informatie door overheids-/toezichtactoren ondanks eventuele geheimhoudingsplichten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 112 verplicht nationale bevoegde autoriteiten op verzoek van de Commissie onverwijld informatie te verstrekken. Artikel 15 beperkt het buiten toepassing laten van geheimhouding tot gevallen waarin informatie of medewerking wordt verlangd wegens de eigen betrokkenheid bij verwerking van persoonsgegevens; die beperking zou niet alle informatieverzoeken onder artikel 112 omvatten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 15 legt geen geheimhoudingsplicht op en verbiedt geen informatieverstrekking; het neemt juist de mogelijkheid weg om zich in de genoemde toezichtssituatie op geheimhouding te beroepen. Artikel 112 bevat daarnaast een zelfstandige, positieve verplichting voor de daarin genoemde instanties om de Commissie informatie te geven, zodat beide voorschriften naast elkaar kunnen worden nageleefd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Geen beroep is mogelijk op een geheimhoudingsplicht, voor zover inlichtingen of medewerking wordt verlangd in verband met de eigen betrokkenheid bij de verwerking van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor de toepassing van de leden 1 tot en met 7 verstrekken de AI-board, de lidstaten en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten onverwijld informatie aan de Commissie op haar verzoek.

verdict.shared_subject: Public authorities' handling and communication of information in regulatory oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 58(b) GDPR empowers a supervisory authority to provide advice to the public on personal-data-protection matters. If the same public body were also a notifying authority holding confidential information about a notified body, public advice based on that information could risk disclosure contrary to Article 45 AI Act.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 58 GDPR confers a power to give advice; it does not require public disclosure of any particular information, much less confidential information. A notifying authority can comply with Article 45 AI Act by keeping information obtained under Article 78 confidential while any GDPR supervisory authority advice remains general or uses non-confidential information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op eigen initiatief dan wel op verzoek, aan het nationaal parlement, aan de regering van de lidstaat, of overeenkomstig het lidstatelijke recht aan andere instellingen en organen alsmede aan het publiek advies te verstrekken over aangelegenheden die verband houden met de bescherming van persoonsgegevens;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Toezicht en audits van essentiële entiteiten, met inbegrip van grensoverschrijdende samenwerking tussen bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 72 kan een Nederlandse bevoegde autoriteit laten eisen dat een essentiële entiteit een onafhankelijke deskundige inschakelt en aanbevelingen uitvoert. Artikel 37 maakt grensoverschrijdende verzoeken om onder meer gerichte beveiligingsaudits mogelijk; in de praktijk kunnen meerdere autoriteiten daardoor auditmaatregelen rond dezelfde entiteit inzetten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen tegengestelde verplichtingen op. Artikel 72 geeft een autoriteit een bevoegdheid jegens de entiteit, terwijl artikel 37 autoriteiten verplicht samen te werken en hun wederzijdse bijstand juist kan omvatten in auditmaatregelen; die samenwerking kan de toepassing van artikel 72 ondersteunen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de resultaten van dat onderzoek binnen een bij het besluit gestelde redelijke termijn te verstrekken aan de bevoegde autoriteit;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in punt c) van de eerste alinea bedoelde wederzijdse bijstand kan betrekking hebben op verzoeken om informatie en toezichtsmaatregelen, met inbegrip van verzoeken om inspecties ter plaatse of toezicht elders of gerichte beveiligingsaudits uit te voeren.

verdict.shared_subject: Cooperation and mutual assistance between competent authorities concerning cross-border services or activities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires consultation before the competent authority rejects a request, while Provision B requires mutual assistance and says a request may not be refused except on specified grounds. In a cross-border medical-device-sector case, one might argue that A adds a rejection procedure that could delay or complicate B’s required assistance.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together: B permits refusal on limited grounds, and A requires consultation before such a refusal. A’s consultation duty is therefore a procedural safeguard consistent with B’s final-sentence consultation requirement, not an incompatible permission to refuse assistance.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Voordat de bevoegde autoriteit het verzoek afwijst, raadpleegt zij de betrokken bevoegde autoriteit van de andere lidstaat van de Europese Unie over de voorgenomen afwijzing en, wanneer de lidstaat daartoe verzoekt, de Europese Commissie en Enisa.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een dergelijk verzoek af te wijzen, raadpleegt de bevoegde autoriteit de andere betrokken bevoegde autoriteiten alsmede, op verzoek van een van de betrokken lidstaten, de Commissie en Enisa.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use notification-related language and impose duties involving information handling, so a superficial reading might suggest that a coordinator handling a vulnerability report and a notifying authority updating a notified-body notification could face competing disclosure or confidentiality requirements. However, neither text requires the same actor to perform incompatible acts, and the provisions concern different institutional roles and subject matters.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires a vulnerability-coordination coordinator to follow up a vulnerability report and preserve the reporter’s anonymity. Provision B requires a notifying authority to inform the Commission and other Member States of relevant changes to a notified body’s notification; these duties can be performed independently without disclosing a vulnerability reporter’s identity.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De coördinator met het oog op een gecoördineerde bekendmaking van kwetsbaarheden geeft opvolging aan de melding door het verrichten van de taken, genoemd in artikel 17, tweede lid, en waarborgt de anonimiteit van de natuurlijke persoon of rechtspersoon die de kwetsbaarheid meldt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit stelt de Commissie en de andere lidstaten via het in artikel 30, lid 2, bedoelde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem in kennis van alle relevante wijzigingen in de aanmelding van een aangemelde instantie.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data, potentially including special-category personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits processing special-category personal data unless one of its listed exceptions applies. Provision B requires a controller to provide information when personal data were not obtained from the data subject, which could require disclosure that special-category data are being processed and of their categories. If the processing is prohibited under A, B's disclosure duty cannot make it lawful, creating a possible tension between disclosure and the prohibition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B regulates transparency for processing that otherwise has a legal basis; it does not authorize or require the underlying processing. Provision A's exceptions can permit special-category processing, after which the controller can comply with B by providing the required information, subject to any applicable exceptions or qualifications not shown here.

verdict.shared_subject: Oversight and audit powers concerning regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address supervisory oversight and require action or documentation connected with oversight. One might argue that an entity subject to the Dutch authority's audit order could also be affected by the lead overseer's inability to conduct oversight outside the Union, creating overlapping supervisory processes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A empowers a competent authority to require an essential entity to obtain an independent audit, provide its results, or implement recommendations. Provision B governs what the lead overseer must do when it cannot conduct oversight activities outside the Union; it does not prohibit, alter, or excuse the entity's compliance with an audit order under Provision A.

verdict.shared_subject: Procedural deadlines under Dutch civil-law proceedings and the GDPR consistency mechanism
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose time-related procedural obligations, but on different actors and in different proceedings: Article 35 governs when a petition may be filed after a controller's response, while GDPR Article 64 governs when the EDPB must issue an opinion after a supervisory authority submits a matter. Their deadlines therefore do not create an incompatible obligation for one actor.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be complied with together because they regulate different procedures, actors, and triggers. A petitioner may file within six weeks (or without a time limit in the stated non-response situation), while the Committee separately issues its opinion within eight weeks, subject to a possible six-week extension.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het verzoekschrift wordt ingediend binnen zes weken na ontvangst van het antwoord van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Dat advies wordt binnen acht weken vastgesteld met gewone meerderheid van de leden van het Comité.

verdict.shared_subject: BWBR0048156: designation of electronic-traffic standards and publication of supervisory/enforcement decisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern formal actions under the same statute and their public accessibility. One could argue that designating a standard under Article 3 requires the standard itself to be publicly accessible, while Article 17 adds a separate publication step for certain decisions, potentially creating uncertainty about what must be published and when.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 3 sets substantive conditions for designating a standard, including that the standard be publicly accessible and free to use. Article 17 requires notification of specified decisions by publication in the Staatscourant; that procedural publication duty does not contradict or alter Article 3's conditions, and both can be fulfilled together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de standaard openbaar toegankelijk en kosteloos bruikbaar is en over de specificaties ervan blijvend vrijelijk kan worden beschikt of waarvan de specificaties blijvend kunnen worden verkregen tegen een redelijke vergoeding.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Van een besluit als bedoeld in het eerste, tweede, vierde en vijfde lid wordt mededeling gedaan door plaatsing in de Staatscourant.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data in connection with prohibited or exceptionally permitted AI practices
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 6 GDPR governs whether further processing of personal data is compatible with the original collection purpose, while Article 5 AI Act prohibits several AI uses, including certain biometric and profiling practices. In a concrete AI deployment, GDPR purpose-compatibility might support or permit processing while Article 5 independently prohibits the AI use, or Article 5 might permit a narrow use while GDPR Article 6 still requires a separate compatibility assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different legal tests and can be complied with cumulatively: Article 6 concerns the lawfulness and purpose compatibility of personal-data processing, whereas Article 5 prohibits specified AI practices regardless of that assessment. A processing operation must satisfy Article 6 and, if it involves an Article 5 practice, also avoid the prohibition or satisfy the expressly stated Article 5 exception; neither text requires conduct that the other forbids.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to classify the provisions as compatible at this level. Article 5's own exceptions and Article 6's other lawfulness requirements may determine a particular case, but the provisions shown do not create an unavoidable conflict.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity information exchange and security measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cybersecurity-related action by public authorities, and information exchanged for a peer review could potentially relate to security measures imposed on communications providers. One might therefore argue that the review-related information exchange could affect or overlap with the Minister’s power to require security measures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires authorities and CSIRTs to exchange information necessary for a NIS2 peer review; it does not regulate or prohibit security measures by communications providers. Provision B merely authorizes the Minister to impose time-limited security-related measures on providers, so the duties and actors can be complied with simultaneously without any incompatible requirement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wisselen de bevoegde autoriteiten, de CSIRT’s en het centrale contactpunt met de cyberbeveiligingsdeskundigen, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn, de informatie uit die noodzakelijk is voor de door de cyberbeveiligingsdeskundigen uit te voeren collegiale toetsing.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan een aanbieder van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten de verplichting opleggen om binnen een bepaalde termijn maatregelen te treffen met betrekking tot onder meer:

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory oversight and conformity-assessment activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a critical ICT third-party provider to submit to on-site inspections ordered by the lead overseer. Provision B requires a notified conformity-assessment body to ensure that subcontractors or subsidiaries performing specific conformity-assessment tasks meet Article 31 requirements and to notify the notifying authority; if the same organisation were subject to both, the inspection duty could involve oversight of activities governed by the subcontracting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors in different regulatory settings: A concerns a critical ICT third-party provider and inspections by a lead overseer, while B concerns a notified conformity-assessment body and its subcontractors or subsidiaries. Nothing in either text requires conduct that prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten onderwerpt zich aan de inspecties ter plaatse die bij besluit van de lead overseer zijn gelast.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-system governance and operational resilience in regulated financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require ICT systems to be managed in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, while attaching that requirement to different organisational and operational duties. A rating agency must maintain effective ICT control and security arrangements, whereas a CTP, trade repository, or other entity must maintain continuity, recovery, or risk-minimisation arrangements; the texts do not establish incompatible benchmarks or obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different regulated entities and impose complementary duties: Provision A concerns rating agencies’ administrative, control, risk-assessment, and ICT security arrangements, while Provision B concerns CCPs and trade repositories’ continuity, recovery, and operational-risk arrangements. Each expressly incorporates the same DORA framework, so both can be satisfied without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and international transfer of personal data, potentially including special-category data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 22 states that the prohibition on processing special-category personal data does not apply in listed circumstances, while Article 49 permits certain transfers of personal data to third countries without adequacy or safeguards. If a transfer involves special-category data, Article 49's transfer derogation does not by itself establish that the underlying processing is exempt from Article 22's prohibition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different legal questions: Article 22 concerns whether processing special-category data is prohibited, whereas Article 49 concerns the additional conditions for transferring personal data to a third country or international organisation. A transfer can comply with both where an Article 22 exception applies and an Article 49 condition is satisfied.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A controller transfers a person's health data to a third-country recipient relying on the data subject's explicit consent under Article 49(1)(a), but the transfer's underlying processing of health data does not clearly fall within any of the Article 22 exceptions shown. The controller therefore has a transfer derogation under Article 49 but no established exception to the special-category processing prohibition under Article 22.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the Article 49 transfer derogation—particularly explicit consent to the transfer under Article 49(1)(a)—also satisfies an applicable Article 9(2) exception to the special-category processing prohibition, as required by Article 22; that legal link is not established by the texts shown.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of traffic/location data and special-category personal data by providers of public electronic communications networks or services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts providers from using retained traffic and location data for other purposes, while Provision B exceptionally permits providers of high-risk AI systems to process special-category personal data for bias detection and correction. If the retained traffic or location data also constitute special-category personal data and are used in such an AI system, B could appear to permit processing that A restricts, subject to A’s own cross-referenced exceptions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B concerns only special-category personal data used for bias detection in specified high-risk AI systems and expressly remains subject to other EU data-protection instruments. Provision A permits other processing where Articles 11.5 and 11.5a allow it; the texts do not establish that B’s processing falls outside those exceptions or that the relevant retained data are special-category data.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a public electronic communications service retains traffic or location data under Article 13.2a, and some of that retained dataset reveals a person’s health status or another Article 9 special category. The provider deploys a high-risk AI system and seeks to process those retained records to detect or correct bias, relying on Article 10 while Article 11.13 restricts processing of the retained data for other purposes.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the processing is permitted under Articles 11.5 and 11.5a, as required by Article 11.13; Article 10 itself does not establish that its exceptional permission for processing special-category data satisfies those provisions’ conditions.

Nothing in the texts makes the scope designation in A incompatible with B's acceptance exception.

An entity can fall within A and the relevant service can simultaneously fall within B; the provisions impose no contradictory command or prohibition.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data for journalistic, academic, artistic, or literary purposes and processing for other purposes without consent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A makes the relevant data-protection law inapplicable to processing exclusively for journalistic or academic, artistic, or literary expression. Provision B prohibits collecting or processing the specified personal data for other purposes without the data subject’s explicit consent, so a processor might view A’s exemption as permitting processing that B otherwise forbids.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: A only removes the application of one law for exclusively expressive purposes, while B independently governs processing of the specified personal data and requires explicit consent for other purposes. The apparent permission under A therefore does not establish that B’s consent requirement is displaced; moreover, the shown text does not identify the data covered by B’s first paragraph or establish that the processing falls within A’s exclusive-purpose exemption.

The publisher may rely on A’s exclusion from the first law, while B appears to prohibit the processing unless consent was obtained; the text shown does not establish whether A overrides B or whether B contains an applicable exception for this journalistic purpose.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the journalistic-purpose exclusion in A also displaces or qualifies B’s separate consent requirement, and whether B’s own exceptions or the omitted first paragraph cover this processing, is not established by the provisions shown.

verdict.shared_subject: Privacy and cybersecurity oversight involving a vulnerability report
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the coordinator to preserve the reporting person's anonymity. The authority can exercise those powers against a controller or processor without contradicting the coordinator's obligation to protect the reporter's anonymity.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing sensitive personal data in automated individual decision-making by a temporary committee or advisory body
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits processing of special-category and criminal-offence data by a committee or advisory body when its listed conditions are met. Provision B requires safeguards, including human intervention, an opportunity to state one’s views, and a right to challenge, so an automated decision using such data could raise an unresolved question whether A’s safeguards are sufficient for B’s individual protections.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different legal requirements rather than incompatible commands: A establishes when sensitive-data processing by a specified body is not prohibited, while B requires protective measures for certain automated decisions. A body can satisfy both by processing only under A’s conditions and providing all measures required by B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A temporary advisory committee lawfully uses health or criminal-offence data in an automated individual decision under A’s conditions, and the decision falls within one of the exceptions referenced in B; the committee must then provide B’s human-intervention, statement-of-views, and challenge rights, but A does not establish that its general safeguards satisfy those specific requirements or that the processing is otherwise covered by the applicable sensitive-data exception.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the processing is covered by the applicable exception to the prohibition on processing special-category or criminal-offence data, including whether the conditions in Article 9(2) and, for criminal-offence data, Article 10 GDPR are satisfied for this automated-decision purpose; the text shown does not establish that link.

verdict.shared_subject: Organisations that provide electronic services and process personal data involving transfers to third countries or international organisations

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose contractual obligations on suppliers involved in regulated systems. However, Article 30 requires specific DORA contract terms for ICT services supporting critical or important functions, while Article 25 requires information, capabilities, technical access and assistance sufficient for full compliance with the AI Act; the texts do not establish that one set of terms necessarily satisfies the other.

However, provision A only extends specified governance rules to each partner of a general partnership, while provision B empowers the Minister to impose a continuity measure on certain providers; the texts impose no incompatible requirement.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A determines who must comply with referenced governance rules when an essential or important entity is a general partnership. Provision B concerns a Ministerial power to require a technical or organisational continuity measure from a specified provider whose continuity plan is inadequate. These duties can plainly coexist and address different triggers and subjects.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together: authorities may exchange information where necessary while preserving confidentiality through controlled, lawful handling and disclosure. Article 70 does not itself prohibit the Article 58 exchange, and Article 78 is not reproduced, so the shown text does not establish an incompatible disclosure rule.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns an exemption from maintaining records of processing activities for certain organisations with fewer than 250 employees, while Provision B requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents. If preparing or submitting an incident report involves processing personal data, the reporting activity may fall within A's exemption while B still requires the report, creating a possible compliance question about documenting that processing.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of special-category personal data for high-risk AI bias detection and correction
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A states that processing special-category personal data is prohibited unless one of its listed exceptions applies. Provision B permits providers of high-risk AI systems to exceptionally process such data for bias detection and correction, but the text shown does not establish that B’s conditions correspond to, or satisfy, any exception in A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be read together: B’s permission is expressly subject to the GDPR, the Law Enforcement Directive, and other applicable rules, while its safeguards may support compliance with A’s exceptions. If the processing has, for example, the data subject’s explicit consent or another applicable exception under A, both provisions can be satisfied.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider processes employees’ ethnic-origin data to detect and correct bias in a high-risk recruitment AI system. The processing may satisfy B’s necessity, minimisation, security, access-control, and deletion conditions, but A still prohibits it unless one of A’s listed exceptions—such as explicit consent—applies; the provisions shown do not establish that B’s permission itself supplies that exception.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the processing falls within one of Provision A’s exceptions to the prohibition, particularly explicit consent under Article 22(a), or another applicable Article 9(2) legal basis; Provision B’s permission and safeguards do not themselves establish that this exception is satisfied.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory authorities’ powers to obtain information or documentation from ICT/AI providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern supervisory access to information and documentation, so an authority or provider operating under both regimes might need to coordinate overlapping requests. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate complementary actors and conduct: A governs cooperation and notification by competent authorities, while B governs the provider’s response to information requests. An authority can notify the oversight forum and the provider can simultaneously provide complete, accurate, and non-misleading information, so both duties can be satisfied together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten zorgen er met name voor dat hun uit hoofde van deze richtlijn bevoegde autoriteiten het oversightforum dat is opgericht op grond van artikel 32, lid 1, van Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 in kennis stellen wanneer zij hun toezichts- en handhavingsbevoegdheden uitoefenen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De vertegenwoordigers van de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten verstrekken de gevraagde informatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Wederzijdse bijstand tussen toezichthoudende/bevoegde autoriteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A makes assistance measures free of charge, while Provision B requires assistance to be provided in proportion to the requested authority’s own resources and permits refusal in specified circumstances. One might therefore question whether costly assistance required under B can be compensated under A, but the texts do not expressly make the assistance obligation and the cost rule incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different aspects of cooperation: A allocates costs for assistance under a GDPR mutual-assistance request, while B requires and structures cooperation for entities operating across Member States under the NIS2 framework. Even where both apply, assistance can be provided under B while remaining free of charge under A; A also expressly allows authorities to agree reimbursement rules for exceptional specific expenses.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De maatregelen die toezichthoudende autoriteiten tot wie een verzoek is gericht nemen uit hoofde van een verzoek om wederzijdse bijstand, zijn kosteloos.
verdict.evidence_span_b: een bevoegde autoriteit, na ontvangst van een gemotiveerd verzoek van een andere bevoegde autoriteit, de andere bevoegde autoriteit wederzijdse bijstand verleent in verhouding tot haar eigen middelen

verdict.shared_subject: Processing personal data, potentially including special-category data, and informing the data subject about further processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts processing of special-category personal data unless one of its listed exceptions applies, while provision B requires information before further processing for a different purpose. If the further processing is prohibited under A, B's information duty does not itself make it lawful; conversely, complying with B may appear to facilitate notice about processing that A forbids.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, sequential duties: A determines whether special-category processing is permitted, while B requires notice when lawfully obtained personal data are further processed for another purpose. A lawful exception under A can coexist with B's notice obligation, and B does not authorize processing or override A.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes confidential data from the Wet open overheid, subject to an environmental-information exception, while Provision B requires Union AI testing structures to provide advice on request. One might speculate that providing advice could involve disclosing confidential information that is excluded from public access, but neither text makes Provision B require public disclosure or identify what information must be supplied.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters: A limits application of an open-government access regime to confidential data, whereas B assigns advisory functions to Union AI testing structures in response to requests from specified authorities. The advisory obligation can be fulfilled without making confidential data publicly accessible, and nothing in B overrides A's confidentiality rule.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Wet open overheid is niet van toepassing op vertrouwelijke gegevens als bedoeld in het eerste lid, behalve voor zover die gegevens milieu-informatie inhouden als bedoeld in artikel 19.1a van de Wet milieubeheer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de ondersteunende AI-teststructuren van de Unie ook onafhankelijk technisch of wetenschappelijk advies op verzoek van de AI-board, de Commissie of markttoezichtautoriteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Information sharing about incidents or breaches by public authorities and designated organisations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require a public authority or related institutional actor to provide information to another institutional recipient about a security-related event. If the same event fell within both regimes, the provisions might appear to create overlapping information-disclosure duties with different recipients and statutory purposes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties on different actors and concern different subject matters: provision A concerns a CSIRT forwarding reports made by certain essential entities, while provision B concerns the Minister supplying information about breaches of secure and reliable access to electronic services when necessary for statutory tasks or services. Nothing in either text forbids the other disclosure or makes compliance with one impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het CSIRT verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging dat overeenkomstig artikel 33, eerste lid, onderdeel a, is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting or notification duties, so a financial entity that also develops or markets a qualifying general-purpose AI model might face two regulatory communications concerning the same broader technology activity. However, the provisions address different triggers, recipients, and subject matter: serious ICT incidents under DORA versus the model’s system-risk qualification under the AI Act.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can plainly be performed together because neither provision forbids or limits compliance with the other. Article 19 applies to financial entities reporting serious ICT-related incidents to competent authorities, while Article 52 applies to providers of qualifying general-purpose AI models notifying the Commission, with different triggering facts and required information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden voldoet aan de in artikel 51, lid 1, punt a), bedoelde voorwaarde, stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT and personal-data security governance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A creates an exception to notifying affected persons when the provider has taken appropriate technical protective measures, such as encryption. Provision B requires a financial entity’s governing body to establish policies ensuring high standards of data confidentiality and to oversee ICT-risk management; one might argue that governance obligations could pressure the entity toward measures that affect whether A’s notification exception is available.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties: A concerns whether a provider must notify individuals after a personal-data breach, subject to an assessment by the Dutch data-protection authority, while B concerns governance and oversight of ICT risk at a financial entity. B does not require notification, prohibit encryption, or establish a conflicting security benchmark, so both can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de invoering van beleidslijnen die erop gericht zijn de handhaving van hoge normen inzake beschikbaarheid, authenticiteit, integriteit en vertrouwelijkheid van gegevens te waarborgen;

verdict.shared_subject: Retention and erasure of traffic and location data by providers of public electronic communications networks or services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts providers from processing traffic and location data retained under Article 13.2a(2) for other purposes, while Provision B gives a data subject a right to obtain erasure and requires the controller to erase personal data in specified circumstances. If the retained data are personal data and a GDPR erasure ground applies, the provider may need to erase data that A regulates, creating a possible interaction between retention-related processing restrictions and erasure duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties rather than contradictory commands: A limits the purposes for which specified retained data may be processed, whereas B requires erasure only when one of its listed conditions applies. Erasure can generally be carried out consistently with A, and B itself excludes erasure where processing is necessary to comply with a legal processing obligation or perform a public-interest task; the texts shown do not establish that the Article 13.2a retention rule requires retaining these data in the relevant scenario.
verdict.missing_reference: The specific Article 13.2a(2) retention obligation and any applicable GDPR Article 17(3)(b) legal-obligation exception would be needed to determine whether retention is legally mandatory despite an erasure request.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 17(3)(b)'s exception for processing necessary to comply with a legal processing obligation, together with the content of Article 13.2a(2), is not established by the provisions shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verkeers- en locatiegegevens die de aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten bewaren op grond van artikel 13.2a, tweede lid, worden door de aanbieders niet voor andere doelen verwerkt, tenzij het gegevens betreft waarvan de verwerking op grond van de artikelen 11.5 en 11.5a is toegestaan en de verwerking plaatsvindt met inachtneming van die artikelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De betrokkene heeft het recht van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging wissing van hem betreffende persoonsgegevens te verkrijgen en de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke is verplicht persoonsgegevens zonder onredelijke vertraging te wissen wanneer een van de volgende gevallen van toepassing is:

verdict.shared_subject: Providing information or documentation to a public authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an entity to transfer or provide information to a public authority, so an entity subject to both might need to determine whether the same stored information must be transferred to the Minister under Provision A and made available to the notifying authority under Provision B. However, the provisions do not impose incompatible content, timing, or confidentiality requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed together: the recognised service can transfer necessary information to the Minister, while a notified body can provide relevant documentation to the notifying authority. The authorities, triggering events, and purposes differ, and nothing in either text forbids making the same information available to both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De erkende dienst waarvan de erkenning wordt ingetrokken of overgedragen draagt er zorg voor dat alle door hem opgeslagen informatie en gegevens die noodzakelijk was voor de uitvoering van de activiteiten waarvoor hij was erkend, worden overgedragen aan Onze Minister.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties stellen alle relevante documentatie, waaronder de documentatie van de aanbieder, ter beschikking van de in artikel 28 bedoelde aanmeldende autoriteit, en verstrekken die aan haar op verzoek, teneinde haar in staat te stellen haar beoordelings-, aanwijzings-, kennisgevings- en monitoringsactiviteiten te verrichten, en de in deze afdeling beschreven beoordeling te vergemakkelijken.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations within EU digital regulation, but they address different actors and regulatory mechanisms. Provision A concerns a lead overseer imposing a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider after non-compliance, whereas Provision B concerns notifying authorities reporting conformity-assessment bodies to the Commission and Member States.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be satisfied simultaneously because they regulate different actors, triggers, and subject matter: a lead overseer may impose a penalty on a critical ICT service provider, while a notifying authority reports a conformity-assessment body through an electronic system. Neither requires or forbids conduct that would prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten melden elke in lid 1 bedoeld conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstantie aan bij de Commissie en de andere lidstaten door middel van het door de Commissie ontwikkelde en beheerde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of special-category personal data and the related processing register
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A establishes when the prohibition on processing special-category personal data does not apply, while provision B requires a controller to record processing activities, including the categories of personal data. A controller might view the register requirement as documenting or facilitating processing that A permits only under specified exceptions. However, B does not itself authorize processing, and A does not prohibit maintaining a legally required register.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, complementary rules: A concerns whether processing special-category data is permitted under specified exceptions, whereas B concerns documenting processing activities and their categories. A controller can comply with B by recording the processing and its legal circumstances while processing only where one of A’s exceptions applies.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het verbod om bijzondere categorieën van persoonsgegevens te verwerken niet van toepassing, indien:

verdict.shared_subject: Acceptance of business and organisational identification means for access to electronic services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits the Minister to designate a non-recognised business or organisational means for access during a specified period. Provision B requires public bodies and designated organisations to accept all and only recognised means and recognised authorisation statements, which appears to exclude that designated non-recognised means.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A is expressly a competence provision and may operate as a statutory exception or authorisation that qualifies the general acceptance duty in provision B. The supplied text does not expressly state whether a designation under A makes the alternative means legally acceptable under B, so the apparent conflict may be resolved by the provision’s legal structure or omitted statutory context.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision establishing the legal effect of a Ministerial designation under Article 15—specifically, whether a means designated under the competence provision is treated as an accepted or recognised means for purposes of the obligation to accept only recognised means and statements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: kan Onze Minister een bedrijfs- of organisatiemiddel aanwijzen dat voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode tevens voor de toegang tot die dienstverlening gebruikt mag worden
verdict.evidence_span_b: accepteren bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties bij de toegang tot hun elektronische dienstverlening alle en uitsluitend erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions both concern institutional responses to risks involving digital systems, but they impose different functions on different actors: the CSIRT must monitor, analyse and assist with cyber incidents, while the supervisory authority may issue GDPR advice within specified periods. No concrete incompatibility or competing benchmark is stated.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The CSIRT provision assigns cybersecurity-monitoring and incident-response tasks to a CSIRT, whereas Article 36 assigns prior-consultation advice and supervisory powers to a data-protection authority concerning proposed personal-data processing. These duties can operate in parallel without requiring either actor to violate the other provision.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau
verdict.evidence_span_b: geeft de toezichthoudende autoriteit binnen een maximumtermijn van acht weken na de ontvangst van het verzoek om raadpleging schriftelijk advies aan de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke

verdict.shared_subject: Processing special-category personal data by an organisation involved in secure electronic public services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision B exceptionally permits high-risk AI providers to process special-category personal data for bias detection and correction, subject to conditions. Provision A requires covered organisations and other listed actors to provide the Minister with data and information needed to prevent or end breaches affecting secure and reliable electronic access; if that information includes special-category personal data, the request could appear to require disclosure that B's conditions restrict, particularly its no-disclosure-to-other-parties condition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not expressly require special-category personal data or regulate its processing; it concerns supplying information to the Minister for electronic-service security measures. Provision B is an exceptional permission, not a general prohibition, and its conditions could potentially be met while responding to A through minimised, pseudonymised or non-sensitive information, so the texts do not establish an actual incompatibility.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A covered organisation operates a high-risk AI system used in electronic public services and, after detecting bias through special-category data, is asked by the Minister under Article 19 to provide the data and information needed to address a security-related incident. The organisation may face a conflict between supplying the underlying special-category data to the Minister and Article 10( d)'s requirement that those data not be transmitted, transferred or otherwise consulted by other parties.
verdict.decisive_exception: The text does not establish whether Article 19's disclosure duty is a legal basis or other applicable exception permitting the Article 10 processing/disclosure of special-category data, nor whether the Minister is an authorised recipient under the relevant GDPR, Law Enforcement Directive or Regulation 2018/1725 rules.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: d) de bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens worden niet verzonden, doorgegeven of anderszins geraadpleegd door andere partijen;

verdict.shared_subject: Electronic access services and possible transfers of personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An erkende ontsluitende dienst must unlock business and organisational means and electronic authorisation statements, which could involve handling personal data. If that service also transfers such data to a third country or international organisation, Article 44 prohibits the transfer unless the GDPR Chapter V conditions are met. Thus, the service obligation could require an operation whose onward transfer is restricted by Article 44.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 13 requires enabling access; it does not require transferring personal data to a third country or international organisation. Article 44 merely conditions such transfers on compliance with Chapter V, so the service can perform its access duty while avoiding an unlawful transfer or satisfying the applicable transfer conditions.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een erkende ontsluitende dienst ontsluit alle erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen, alle door erkende machtigingsdiensten afgegeven elektronische verklaringen waaruit blijkt dat een natuurlijke persoon, onderneming of rechtspersoon gemachtigd is namens de onderneming of rechtspersoon, bedoeld in artikel 15, eerste lid, op te treden bij de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening en alle op grond van artikel 12 aangewezen attributen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan; dit geldt ook voor verdere doorgiften van persoonsgegevens vanuit het derde land of een internationale organisatie aan een ander derde land of een andere internationale organisatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Uitsluitend geautomatiseerde individuele besluitvorming die iemand rechtsgevolgen heeft of anderszins in aanmerkelijke mate treft
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 22 lid 1 formuleert een recht van de betrokkene om niet aan zo’n besluit te worden onderworpen, terwijl artikel 40 een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke toestaat de besluitvorming onder voorwaarden voort te zetten mits passende beschermingsmaatregelen worden getroffen. Op het eerste gezicht kan daardoor onduidelijk lijken of maatregelen de besluitvorming zelf kunnen rechtvaardigen of alleen de gevolgen ervan moeten beperken.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn verenigbaar omdat artikel 40 uitdrukkelijk ziet op een uitzondering op het verbod van artikel 22 en passende maatregelen als voorwaarde stelt. De context bepaalt bovendien dat artikel 22 lid 2(b) een wettelijke uitzondering toestaat wanneer de toepasselijke bepaling zelf passende maatregelen voorschrijft; artikel 40 vult juist die waarborg in, zodat het individuele recht niet wordt genegeerd maar via voorwaarden wordt beschermd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij de geautomatiseerde individuele besluitvorming, bedoeld in het eerste lid, treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke passende maatregelen die strekken tot bescherming van de rechten en vrijheden en gerechtvaardigde belangen van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De betrokkene heeft het recht niet te worden onderworpen aan een uitsluitend op geautomatiseerde verwerking, waaronder profilering, gebaseerd besluit waaraan voor hem rechtsgevolgen zijn verbonden of dat hem anderszins in aanmerkelijke mate treft.

verdict.shared_subject: Information handled by a data protection officer versus information supplied to the European Commission under the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern disclosure of information, so a data protection officer could conceivably possess information obtained from a data subject's complaint or request that is relevant to an AI Act evaluation. Article 39 requires secrecy unless the data subject consents, while Article 112 requires the listed authorities and AI Board to provide information to the Commission without delay when requested.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors and duties: Article 39 binds the data protection officer, whereas Article 112 binds the AI Board, Member States, and national competent authorities. Article 112 therefore does not require a data protection officer to disclose anything, and the authorities can comply using information they are lawfully entitled to provide without breaching the officer's separate confidentiality duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De functionaris voor gegevensbescherming, bedoeld in de artikelen 37 tot en met 39 van de verordening, is verplicht tot geheimhouding van hetgeen hem op grond van een klacht of een verzoek van betrokkene is bekend geworden, tenzij de betrokkene in bekendmaking toestemt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor de toepassing van de leden 1 tot en met 7 verstrekken de AI-board, de lidstaten en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten onverwijld informatie aan de Commissie op haar verzoek.

verdict.shared_subject: Access to confidential information or AI-model materials by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes confidential data from the Wet open overheid, subject to an environmental-information exception, while Provision B empowers the Commission to request access to a general-purpose AI model, potentially including source code. If the requested model materials are confidential data held by a Dutch public body, the access request could appear to collide with the exclusion in A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the applicability of the Dutch open-government disclosure regime, whereas Provision B concerns the Commission’s competence to request access for evaluations under the AI Act. A Commission request is not necessarily a Woo disclosure, and the texts do not establish that the requested model or source code is confidential data covered by A or that the Dutch body may refuse a binding EU-law request on that basis.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Wet open overheid is niet van toepassing op vertrouwelijke gegevens als bedoeld in het eerste lid, behalve voor zover die gegevens milieu-informatie inhouden als bedoeld in artikel 19.1a van de Wet milieubeheer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: kan de Commissie verzoeken om toegang tot het betrokken AI-model voor algemene doeleinden via API’s of andere passende technische middelen en instrumenten, waaronder de broncode.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory compliance obligations concerning ICT and conformity-assessment bodies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires detection mechanisms to support incident-response activation, while Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application to a notifying authority. One might argue that both concern organisational compliance processes, but the texts impose different duties with no apparent incompatibility.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address distinct subject matters and duties: A concerns technical ICT-incident detection and response mechanisms, whereas B concerns where a conformity-assessment body must submit an application. An entity subject to both could satisfy both requirements without either affecting the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde detectiemechanismen maken meerdere controlelagen mogelijk en bepalen waarschuwingsdrempels en criteria om processen voor respons op ICT-gerelateerde incidenten in werking te stellen, met inbegrip van automatische waarschuwingsmechanismen voor de betrokken personeelsleden die belast zijn met de respons op ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Wederzijdse bijstand tussen toezichthoudende autoriteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 37 verplicht de aangezochte autoriteit in beginsel bijstand te verlenen en zegt dat zij een verzoek niet mag weigeren behalve op limitatief genoemde gronden. Artikel 61 AVG staat weigering toe wanneer het verzoek inbreuk maakt op de AVG of op toepasselijk Unierecht of nationaal recht, zodat een verzoek dat onder artikel 37 valt maar volgens de ontvangende autoriteit zulke regels schendt, tot een botsing kan leiden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen worden gelezen als samenwerkende regels: artikel 37 verplicht bijstand binnen de bevoegdheid, proportionaliteit en veiligheidsgrenzen die het zelf noemt, terwijl artikel 61 een AVG-specifieke weigeringsgrond bevat. Artikel 37 kan bovendien worden toegepast zonder afbreuk te doen aan hogere of toepasselijke Unierechtelijke beperkingen, zodat niet vaststaat dat elk artikel-37-verzoek ook onder artikel 61 moet worden geweigerd.
verdict.missing_reference: De ontbrekende beslissende bepaling is de voorrangs- of verenigbaarheidsregel die bepaalt of artikel 37 van Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 een verzoek verplicht ondanks artikel 61, onder b, AVG, of juist toestaat dat een AVG-strijdig verzoek wordt geweigerd. Ook is de concrete inhoud van het verzoek nodig om vast te stellen of het daadwerkelijk inbreuk maakt op de AVG of ander toepasselijk recht.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het verzoek inbreuk maakt op deze verordening of met Unierecht of lidstatelijk recht dat van toepassing is op de toezichthoudende autoriteit die het verzoek ontvangt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bevoegde autoriteit waaraan een verzoek om bijstand is gericht, mag dat verzoek niet weigeren, tenzij wordt vastgesteld dat zij niet bevoegd is om de gevraagde bijstand te verlenen, dat de gevraagde bijstand niet in verhouding staat tot de toezichthoudende taken van de bevoegde autoriteit, of dat het verzoek betrekking heeft op informatie of activiteiten inhoudt die, indien ze openbaar zouden worden gemaakt of zouden worden uitgevoerd, in strijd zouden zijn met de wezenlijke belangen van zijn nationale veiligheid, de openbare veiligheid of de defensie van die lidstaat.

verdict.shared_subject: Confidentiality of information obtained by authorities under EU digital-law regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits disclosure of information covered by professional secrecy to any other person or authority unless Union or national law provides otherwise. Provision B requires notifying authorities to ensure confidentiality of information obtained under Article 78; if that information is also covered by professional secrecy, both provisions point toward non-disclosure rather than imposing incompatible conduct.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together: Provision B requires notifying authorities to treat Article 78 information confidentially, while Provision A independently restricts disclosure of information covered by professional secrecy and expressly allows disclosure where Union or national law provides for it. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different, independently defined categories: A concerns high-risk AI systems, especially those intended for public-authority use, while B concerns components of large-scale IT systems established under the listed legal acts. If the requested material contains personal data and must be sent to an authority outside the GDPR transfer framework, complying with B could entail a transfer that A does not permit.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different immediate matters: B requires cooperation with competent authorities, whereas A permits international transfers when its Chapter V conditions are satisfied. B does not expressly require an international transfer or override GDPR safeguards, so a provider can comply by supplying non-personal information, using a lawful transfer mechanism, or otherwise responding without violating A.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, sequentially compatible rules: A determines who is subject to governance requirements, while B concerns a temporary enforcement measure triggered by unresolved deficiencies. Nothing in A requires that person to remain in office or forbids a temporary management ban, and B expressly provides procedural safeguards and applies only under specified conditions.

verdict.shared_subject: Telecommunications data disclosure and exemptions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the legal framework for handling a request for disclosure and an exemption, but neither text creates an incompatible command. One might therefore question whether individual partners, rather than the entity, must report significant incidents. The entity can report while its partners separately comply with the applicable governance rules; neither provision requires or forbids conduct inconsistent with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a public identification means and ICT continuity registers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A possible connection is that an organisation using the public identification means might also be a financial entity subject to DORA, and its continuity or recovery activities could involve access to electronic services. Article 8 restricts the identification means to access to specified public electronic services, while Article 11 requires registers during activated ICT continuity or recovery plans; if those registers required use of the identification means for a non-permitted purpose, the duties could appear to pull in different directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different conduct: Article 8 limits the purposes for which a public identification means and related facility may be used, whereas Article 11 requires financial entities to keep accessible registers of activities before and during disruptions. The register duty does not require use of the public identification means, and the texts do not establish that such use is necessary or that the registers concern access to the covered public services.

verdict.shared_subject: An authorised representative’s handling of personal data and compliance documentation when a high-risk AI provider is established in a third country and transfers that data or documentation to the EU.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 44 restricts transfers of personal data to a third country or international organisation unless the GDPR Chapter V conditions are met. Article 22 requires the representative to retain and provide documentation and logs to authorities, which could involve transferring personal data, but Article 22 itself does not state that such transfers satisfy Article 44’s conditions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties rather than contradictory commands: Article 22 requires compliance-related records and information to be made available, while Article 44 permits the transfer if its separate Chapter V conditions are fulfilled. The representative can therefore perform Article 22 through a lawful transfer mechanism, or provide non-personal documentation where applicable.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A representative in the EU for a third-country provider receives automatically generated logs containing identifiable individuals’ data and transfers them to the provider or an authority in another third country to fulfil an Article 22 request, while no GDPR Chapter V transfer condition has been established. Article 22 calls for the information to be provided, whereas Article 44 prohibits the transfer absent the required conditions.
verdict.decisive_exception: The applicable GDPR Chapter V transfer condition or safeguard under Article 44 (for example, an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards, or a relevant derogation) is not established by the texts shown.

verdict.shared_subject: Disclosure of information and documentation in regulatory contexts
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information being made available, but they impose duties toward different recipients and serve different functions: Article 15 gives the data subject a right to be informed about safeguards for a third-country transfer, while Article 34 requires notified bodies to provide documentation to a notifying authority. Nothing in either text says that complying with one duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are readily cumulative: a controller can inform the data subject about the Article 46 safeguards and a notified body can separately provide relevant documentation to the notifying authority on request. Their actors, recipients, triggers, and purposes differ, and neither provision limits the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The strongest possible tension case is that a service provider might be both an entity eligible for exemption from obligations under one regime and a service requiring recognition under the other. However, Provision A concerns a ministerial power to exempt certain entities from obligations in Article 21, while Provision B concerns recognition of specified services subject to rules set by general administrative order; neither text makes compliance with one condition incompatible with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions operate on different legal objects and mechanisms: A authorizes an exemption for an essential or important entity carrying out specified activities or serving a government body, whereas B requires ministerial recognition of an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst meeting separately established rules. An entity could receive an exemption and still seek or hold recognition, because nothing in either text forbids simultaneous application.

verdict.shared_subject: Recognition withdrawal and transitional-law applicability
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern recognised services or parties within an electronic-access framework. One might argue that a recognised service seeking withdrawal must submit a termination plan, while the other excludes certain private-system parties from the transitional regime, potentially affecting whether recognition-related rules apply.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 14 governs the voluntary withdrawal of an existing recognition and the accompanying termination plan. Article 24(3) instead states that its transitional provision does not apply to parties conducting only level-1 activities; it neither forbids withdrawal nor excuses or alters the termination-plan requirement.

verdict.shared_subject: Member States’ sanctioning rules and notification duties under the GDPR
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require Member States to establish or apply sanctions that are effective, proportionate, and dissuasive, and both require notification to the Commission by 25 May 2018. A possible tension is that Article 83 concerns administrative fines, while Article 84 concerns other sanctions, creating a potential boundary question where an infringement might be subject to either category.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions expressly address different sanction categories: Article 83 governs administrative fines, including their judicial imposition where necessary, while Article 84 governs other sanctions, particularly infringements not subject to administrative fines under Article 83. Their common effectiveness, proportionality, dissuasiveness, and notification requirements can be satisfied simultaneously, and the contextual paragraph confirms the same notification deadline for Article 84.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative fines for overlapping data-protection and AI-law infringements
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits the competent authority from imposing a second fine for the same conduct after a GDPR fine under Article 58(2)(i). Provision B authorizes the European Data Protection Supervisor to impose administrative fines on EU institutions and bodies, potentially creating an apparent overlap if the same conduct also falls within the AI Regulation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different authorities, addressees, and legal regimes: A concerns a competent authority and duplication of fines under specified Dutch/GDPR enforcement provisions, while B concerns the EDPS fining EU institutions, bodies, and agencies under the AI Regulation. Nothing in the texts establishes that the same authority, person, conduct, or fines are covered by both provisions, so they can operate independently.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data by a processor or person acting under a controller’s or processor’s authority, including special-category data in a high-risk AI system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a processor or person acting under the controller’s or processor’s authority to process personal data only on the controller’s instructions, unless Union or Member State law requires the processing. Provision B exceptionally permits high-risk AI providers to process special-category personal data for bias detection and correction, so a provider or processor could face uncertainty if the AI Act permission is not itself treated as a Union-law obligation or sufficient instruction under Provision A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together: the provider can process the special-category data only on the controller’s documented instructions, while complying with all of Provision B’s necessity, security, access-control, deletion, and documentation conditions. Provision B expressly operates alongside Regulation 2016/679, and its permission need not displace Provision A’s instruction requirement.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider operating a high-risk AI system uses identifiable health data to detect and correct bias after determining that anonymised or synthetic data cannot work effectively. The provider is acting as a processor under a controller’s authority, but the controller has not instructed or authorised this special-category-data processing; the provider must therefore determine whether Provision B’s exceptional permission and Union-law status allow it to proceed despite Provision A’s instruction-only rule.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the exceptional permission in Provision B constitutes a Union-law obligation or otherwise satisfies the instruction/authorisation requirement in Provision A, and whether the GDPR special-category-data exception applicable to the processing is established. The texts shown do not resolve that legal-basis and instruction link.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity and serious-incident governance involving a national cyber-crisis authority and an AI-system market-surveillance authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related governance, but they assign functions to different authorities and do not state how those functions interact. A possible operational overlap exists if a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system is also a large-scale cybersecurity incident covered by the national plan, potentially creating uncertainty about coordination or responsibility.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A merely designates the Minister and assigns the tasks contained in the national plan, while Provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to take measures within seven days after receiving a notification and follow Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 procedures. The provisions impose no incompatible command, deadline, or prohibition, and their different authorities and triggers can operate concurrently.
