verdict.evidence_span_b: brengt hij het AI-systeem met een hoog risico niet in de handel voordat het in overeenstemming is gebracht met deze eisen

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions impose obligations under different regulatory regimes: Article 36 requires a controller to consult a data-protection authority before certain high-risk personal-data processing, while Article 48 concerns CE-marking identification for a high-risk AI system. One might argue that a provider could need to complete both procedures before deployment, creating additional regulatory burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations have different subjects, triggers, purposes, and acts required. Article 36 concerns a controller and prior consultation triggered by a data-protection impact assessment showing high risk absent mitigation; Article 48 concerns CE-marking and identification of a notified body where applicable. Compliance with one neither prevents nor substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien van toepassing, wordt de CE-markering gevolgd door het identificatienummer van de aangemelde instantie

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and registration of data relating to regulated systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts providers from processing retained traffic and location data for other purposes, except where processing is permitted under the specified provisions. Provision B requires an AI provider or authorised representative to enter specified data in an EU database, so a provider might need to use data that falls within A's prohibition to fulfil B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different data and duties: A concerns traffic and location data retained under article 13.2a, while B concerns the data listed in Annex VIII for certain high-risk AI systems. Nothing in B expressly requires processing the particular retained communications data covered by A, and B can be fulfilled using the required Annex VIII data in a manner permitted by A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verkeers- en locatiegegevens die de aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten bewaren op grond van artikel 13.2a, tweede lid, worden door de aanbieders niet voor andere doelen verwerkt
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in afdelingen A en B van bijlage VIII vermelde gegevens worden in de EU-databank ingevoerd door de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gemachtigde.

verdict.shared_subject: Delegated authority to make further rules by algemene maatregel van bestuur
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions confer competence to adopt further rules by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur, so one might initially suspect overlapping delegated rule-making powers. However, they concern different statutory provisions and no text says that exercising one competence would prevent or contradict exercising the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A authorises additional criteria for determining when an incident is significant for specified NIS2 entities, while provision B generally permits further rules concerning its own article. These competences can be exercised cumulatively and do not impose incompatible duties, permissions, or standards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: kunnen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur naast de hiervoor bedoelde specificaties in uitvoeringshandelingen, aanvullende criteria worden vastgesteld
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen nadere regels worden gesteld ten aanzien van het bepaalde in dit artikel.

verdict.shared_subject: Information sharing about incidents or breaches in electronic services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an authority to disclose information to other public bodies or designated organisations. If the same information concerned a significant incident affecting electronic public services, one might initially question whether the two disclosure regimes impose different recipient, necessity, or procedural requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulative information-sharing duties on different authorities and for different statutory purposes. Article 40 concerns information about a reported significant incident involving an essential entity that is also a critical entity, while Article 19 concerns data and information about a breach of secure and reliable access to electronic services insofar as necessary for recipients' statutory tasks; nothing in either text forbids compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.

verdict.shared_subject: Oversight and information duties concerning critical third-party ICT service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the same critical third-party ICT service providers and their regulatory oversight. One could argue that cooperation and notification under Provision A might create an additional procedural burden or disclosure context, while Provision B requires the provider to supply requested information and remain responsible for its accuracy.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A imposes a duty on Member State authorities to cooperate and notify the oversight forum when exercising supervisory or enforcement powers. Provision B imposes a separate duty on representatives of critical third-party ICT providers to provide requested information, with optional representation by authorised lawyers and continuing provider responsibility; the duties can plainly be performed together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten zorgen ervoor dat hun uit hoofde van deze richtlijn bevoegde autoriteiten samenwerken met de relevante uit hoofde van Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 bevoegde autoriteiten van de betrokken lidstaat.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De vertegenwoordigers van de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten verstrekken de gevraagde informatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Information about cybersecurity incidents and threats in electronic public services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information flows involving incidents or threats, so one might initially suspect that the CSIRT's handling of voluntary reports could overlap with the Minister's duty to provide information about breaches to designated bodies or service providers. However, neither text requires the same actor to take incompatible action, and the provisions regulate different information channels and duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the CSIRT to process voluntary reports under its statutory procedure and expressly allows it to prioritise mandatory reports over voluntary ones. Provision B requires the Minister to provide necessary information about breaches to specified recipients for the performance of their statutory tasks; the CSIRT's processing priority does not prevent or contradict that disclosure duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and transparency concerning personal data, including special-category data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A makes processing special-category personal data permissible only where one of the listed Article 9(2) grounds applies. Provision B requires information before further processing for a new purpose, but that information duty does not itself establish a lawful basis for the special-category processing; thus an operator might comply with B while still violating A, although the provisions do not command opposite conduct.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible requirements: where further processing of special-category data is otherwise lawful under one of A’s exceptions, the controller can both rely on that exception and provide the information required by B before the further processing. B neither authorises processing nor requires processing that A prohibits.

verdict.shared_subject: Information sharing about incidents or breaches by public authorities and related entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require information to be supplied to other public bodies or designated organisations, so an incident or access-security breach could potentially fall within both information-sharing regimes. However, neither text prohibits the disclosure required by the other, imposes incompatible content or deadlines, or makes compliance with one substitute for compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 40 requires the CSIRT to provide information about a reported incident, near-incident or cyber threat concerning an essential entity that is also a critical entity to the competent authority under the Critical Entities Resilience Act. Article 19 separately requires the Minister to provide data and information about a breach of secure and reliable access to electronic services where necessary for recipients' statutory tasks or services; both duties can be performed cumulatively by the relevant actors.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het CSIRT verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging dat overeenkomstig artikel 33, eerste lid, onderdeel a, is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes confidential data from the Wet open overheid, while provision B requires Union AI testing structures to provide independent technical or scientific advice. If that advice request involved confidential information, disclosure or use of such information might appear difficult to reconcile with the exclusion in A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A regulates the applicability of the Dutch open-government disclosure regime to confidential data; it does not prohibit every disclosure or use of confidential data. Provision B imposes an advice duty on Union AI testing structures and does not itself require disclosure under the Wet open overheid, so both provisions can operate without conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Wet open overheid is niet van toepassing op vertrouwelijke gegevens als bedoeld in het eerste lid, behalve voor zover die gegevens milieu-informatie inhouden als bedoeld in artikel 19.1a van de Wet milieubeheer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de ondersteunende AI-teststructuren van de Unie ook onafhankelijk technisch of wetenschappelijk advies op verzoek van de AI-board, de Commissie of markttoezichtautoriteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Geautomatiseerde individuele besluitvorming waarop artikel 22 AVG van toepassing is
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 22 AVG formulates a right not to be subjected to certain solely automated decisions, while Article 40 requires the controller to take appropriate protective measures when the prohibition does not apply under its referenced exception. Read in isolation, this could appear to permit the decision subject to safeguards rather than prohibit the decision outright.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions operate as a general prohibition with an exception, not as contradictory commands: Article 40 applies only to automated individual decision-making covered by the exception in Article 40(1), which states that Article 22(1) does not apply where the decision is necessary for a legal obligation or public-interest task. The required safeguards—potentially including human intervention, the opportunity to state one's view, and the right to challenge—can therefore be satisfied alongside the applicable exception.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij de geautomatiseerde individuele besluitvorming, bedoeld in het eerste lid, treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke passende maatregelen die strekken tot bescherming van de rechten en vrijheden en gerechtvaardigde belangen van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De betrokkene heeft het recht niet te worden onderworpen aan een uitsluitend op geautomatiseerde verwerking, waaronder profilering, gebaseerd besluit waaraan voor hem rechtsgevolgen zijn verbonden of dat hem anderszins in aanmerkelijke mate treft.

verdict.shared_subject: Acceptance of identification means for access to electronic services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A allows the Minister to designate a non-recognised business or organisational means for access to specified electronic services during a specified period. Provision B requires bodies and designated organisations to accept all and exclusively recognised means and recognised authorisation statements, which could appear to exclude the designated non-recognised means.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are expressly part of the same statutory scheme and A is a specific competence to designate an alternative means for particular services, periods and organisations, while B states the ordinary acceptance rule. A can therefore operate as a statutory exception or qualification to B, especially because B begins with “Onverminderd het bepaalde in artikel 7” and the supplied context identifies further qualifications within Article 15. The texts do not establish that the Minister’s designation must be ignored despite B.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 15(5)-(6), or another provision of the instrument, expressly makes a Ministerial designation under A an exception to B’s exclusivity rule is not fully reproduced. Nevertheless, the provisions are best read as an ordinary competence-plus-acceptance structure rather than as an established impossibility of simultaneous compliance.
verdict.evidence_span_a: kan Onze Minister een bedrijfs- of organisatiemiddel aanwijzen dat voor een bij dat besluit te bepalen periode tevens voor de toegang tot die dienstverlening gebruikt mag worden
verdict.evidence_span_b: accepteren bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties bij de toegang tot hun elektronische dienstverlening alle en uitsluitend erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen

verdict.shared_subject: Retention and processing of traffic and location data by public electronic-communications providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 11.13 prohibits providers from processing traffic and location data retained under Article 13.2a for other purposes, while GDPR Article 17 can require a controller to erase personal data without undue delay when one of its listed grounds applies. If erasure is itself a form of processing or the provider must retain the data to comply with Article 11.13, the provisions might appear to pull in different directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be obeyed cumulatively: the provider may erase the retained data when Article 17 requires it, while Article 11.13 governs the purposes for which data that remains retained may be processed. Moreover, Article 17(3)(b) expressly excludes erasure where processing is necessary to comply with a legal processing obligation, and Article 11.13 itself permits processing where Articles 11.5 and 11.5a allow it.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 17(3)(b)'s exception for processing necessary to comply with a statutory processing obligation, together with the legal characterization of erasure as processing, would be relevant if retention under Article 13.2a were claimed to override erasure; the provisions shown do not establish that retention obligation as such an exception, but no actual incompatibility follows because Article 11.13 does not require retention or prohibit erasure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verkeers- en locatiegegevens die de aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten bewaren op grond van artikel 13.2a, tweede lid, worden door de aanbieders niet voor andere doelen verwerkt
verdict.evidence_span_b: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke is verplicht persoonsgegevens zonder onredelijke vertraging te wissen wanneer een van de volgende gevallen van toepassing is:

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for entities that may fall within both the financial-entity and general-purpose AI-provider regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification or reporting duties to public authorities, and a financial entity that is also a provider of a qualifying general-purpose AI model could face two separate immediate-notification regimes. However, the duties concern different triggering events, recipients, and information, and nothing in the texts makes compliance with one impossible or substitutes one for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A financial entity must report serious ICT-related incidents under Provision A, while a provider must notify the Commission when its general-purpose AI model meets the referenced system-risk condition under Provision B. An actor subject to both can submit both notifications to the respective authorities; the provisions contain no incompatible deadline, content requirement, or prohibition on dual reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden voldoet aan de in artikel 51, lid 1, punt a), bedoelde voorwaarde, stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Providing documentation or information to a competent authority for regulatory oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an entity to provide stored information or relevant documentation to a public authority. If the same entity and material fall within both regimes, the provisions could appear to impose overlapping transfer or disclosure duties to different authorities, potentially raising a question about which authority should receive the material.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: provision A concerns an erkende dienst whose recognition is withdrawn or transferred and requires transfer to the Minister, while provision B concerns notified bodies and requires relevant documentation to the notifying authority on request for specified oversight activities. Neither provision forbids disclosure to the other authority, and they concern different triggers, authorities, and potentially different categories of material.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De erkende dienst waarvan de erkenning wordt ingetrokken of overgedragen draagt er zorg voor dat alle door hem opgeslagen informatie en gegevens die noodzakelijk was voor de uitvoering van de activiteiten waarvoor hij was erkend, worden overgedragen aan Onze Minister.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties stellen alle relevante documentatie, waaronder de documentatie van de aanbieder, ter beschikking van de in artikel 28 bedoelde aanmeldende autoriteit, en verstrekken die aan haar op verzoek, teneinde haar in staat te stellen haar beoordelings-, aanwijzings-, kennisgevings- en monitoringsactiviteiten te verrichten, en de in deze afdeling beschreven beoordeling te vergemakkelijken.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations under EU digital regulation, so a superficial comparison might suggest overlapping compliance burdens. However, provision A concerns a lead overseer compelling a critical ICT third-party provider through a penalty payment, while provision B concerns notifying conformity-assessment bodies to the Commission and Member States.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, procedures, and subject matters: A authorises a lead overseer to impose a coercive fine for non-compliance with oversight measures, whereas B requires notifying authorities to report eligible conformity-assessment bodies. Compliance with one does not prevent or interfere with compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten melden elke in lid 1 bedoeld conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstantie aan bij de Commissie en de andere lidstaten door middel van het door de Commissie ontwikkelde en beheerde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and disclosure of personal data in electronic public services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an accredited disclosing service to disclose all accredited business and organisational means, electronic authorisation statements, and designated attributes. If carrying out that duty entails transferring personal data to a third country or international organisation, Provision B permits that transfer only after the GDPR Chapter V conditions have been met, so A could appear to require disclosure where B restricts it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not require an international transfer or otherwise exempt the service from data-protection rules; it can be performed through a disclosure that complies with Provision B. Provision B expressly operates alongside other applicable rules, and its conditions can therefore be treated as cumulative requirements for any transfer rather than as a prohibition on the disclosures required by A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een erkende ontsluitende dienst ontsluit alle erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen, alle door erkende machtigingsdiensten afgegeven elektronische verklaringen waaruit blijkt dat een natuurlijke persoon, onderneming of rechtspersoon gemachtigd is namens de onderneming of rechtspersoon, bedoeld in artikel 15, eerste lid, op te treden bij de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening en alle op grond van artikel 12 aangewezen attributen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan; dit geldt ook voor verdere doorgiften van persoonsgegevens vanuit het derde land of een internationale organisatie aan een ander derde land of een andere internationale organisatie.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions involve regulatory oversight of digital systems, but they impose duties on different actors and address different functions: the CSIRT monitors cyber threats and may assist an entity, while the supervisory authority gives GDPR consultation advice and may exercise enforcement powers. Nothing in either text requires one actor to act contrary to the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are readily cumulative: a CSIRT can monitor threats, analyse incidents, or assist an entity while a data-protection supervisory authority separately handles prior consultation concerning a proposed processing operation. The CSIRT provision contains no prohibition on GDPR consultation, and Article 36 contains no restriction on CSIRT activities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau
verdict.evidence_span_b: geeft de toezichthoudende autoriteit binnen een maximumtermijn van acht weken na de ontvangst van het verzoek om raadpleging schriftelijk advies aan de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke

verdict.shared_subject: Information handled by public or regulatory actors
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the data protection officer to keep information obtained through a complaint or data-subject request confidential, unless the data subject consents to disclosure. Provision B requires the AI Board, Member States and national competent authorities to provide information to the Commission on request, so an authority could theoretically request information that originated from such a complaint.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different situations: A governs the data protection officer's confidentiality, while B concerns information held by the AI Board, Member States and national competent authorities for the AI Act's evaluation. Nothing in B expressly requires disclosure of information covered by A, and the duties can be satisfied by providing non-confidential or otherwise lawfully disclosable information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De functionaris voor gegevensbescherming, bedoeld in de artikelen 37 tot en met 39 van de verordening, is verplicht tot geheimhouding van hetgeen hem op grond van een klacht of een verzoek van betrokkene is bekend geworden, tenzij de betrokkene in bekendmaking toestemt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor de toepassing van de leden 1 tot en met 7 verstrekken de AI-board, de lidstaten en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten onverwijld informatie aan de Commissie op haar verzoek.

verdict.shared_subject: Confidentiality and disclosure of information held by authorities under EU digital-law regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits providing information covered by professional secrecy to any other person or authority unless Union or national law provides a basis. Provision B requires notifying authorities to ensure confidentiality of information obtained under Article 78, which could be read as imposing a confidentiality duty over information that another regime might require to be disclosed.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose compatible confidentiality obligations on different authorities and do not require disclosure. Provision B's duty to keep information confidential can be fulfilled consistently with Provision A's prohibition, while any disclosure permitted by Union or national law under Provision A would not necessarily violate B if confidentiality is maintained subject to the applicable legal framework.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onder het beroepsgeheim vallende informatie, waaronder de uitwisseling van informatie tussen de bevoegde autoriteiten uit hoofde van deze verordening en de overeenkomstig Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 aangewezen of ingestelde bevoegde autoriteiten, wordt aan geen enkele andere persoon of autoriteit verstrekt, tenzij op grond van Unierechtelijke of nationaalrechtelijke bepalingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns ICT-incident detection mechanisms and response alerts, while Provision B concerns the submission of an application by conformity-assessment bodies to a notifying authority. No actor, duty, trigger, or subject matter is shared in a way that creates an incompatibility.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose separate obligations on different subjects and address unrelated regulatory functions: incident-detection controls under A and notification applications by conformity-assessment bodies under B. An entity can comply with both without either rule affecting the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde detectiemechanismen maken meerdere controlelagen mogelijk en bepalen waarschuwingsdrempels en criteria om processen voor respons op ICT-gerelateerde incidenten in werking te stellen, met inbegrip van automatische waarschuwingsmechanismen voor de betrokken personeelsleden die belast zijn met de respons op ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Access to confidential information or AI-model materials by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes confidential data from the Wet open overheid, subject to an environmental-information exception. Provision B empowers the Commission to request access to a general-purpose AI model, potentially including source code, so an access request could concern confidential material that is excluded from disclosure under A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different mechanisms and actors: A concerns the applicability of Dutch open-government disclosure rules to confidential data, while B concerns the Commission’s investigative competence under the AI Act. B does not itself require disclosure under the Wet open overheid, and A does not prohibit a separate, legally authorised Commission request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Wet open overheid is niet van toepassing op vertrouwelijke gegevens als bedoeld in het eerste lid, behalve voor zover die gegevens milieu-informatie inhouden als bedoeld in artikel 19.1a van de Wet milieubeheer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: kan de Commissie verzoeken om toegang tot het betrokken AI-model voor algemene doeleinden via API’s of andere passende technische middelen en instrumenten, waaronder de broncode.

verdict.shared_subject: AI-systemen die vóór de toepasselijke datum in de handel zijn gebracht of in gebruik zijn gesteld
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen op hetzelfde AI-systeem van toepassing zijn, maar leggen dan verschillende uiterste nalevingsdata op: 2 augustus 2030 voor bepaalde hoogrisicosystemen die door overheidsinstanties worden gebruikt, tegenover 31 december 2030 voor AI-systemen die componenten zijn van bepaalde grootschalige IT-systemen. Dat kan een temporele spanning opleveren als één systeem onder beide omschrijvingen valt, hoewel de teksten niet uitdrukkelijk bepalen welke termijn voorrang heeft.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen hebben verschillende toepassingsvoorwaarden en kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: een systeem dat onder beide valt, kan uiterlijk op 2 augustus 2030 aan de verordening voldoen en voldoet daarmee ook aan de latere termijn van 31 december 2030. Bovendien kan de verwijzing naar overheidsgebruik in A een andere categorie afbakenen dan de verwijzing naar componenten van grootschalige IT-systemen in B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In ieder geval ondernemen de aanbieders en gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico die bedoeld zijn om door overheidsinstanties te worden gebruikt, de nodige stappen om uiterlijk op 2 augustus 2030 aan de eisen en verplichtingen van deze verordening te voldoen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: AI-systemen die componenten zijn van de bij de in bijlage X vermelde rechtshandelingen opgezette grootschalige IT-systemen die vóór 2 augustus 2027 in de handel zijn gebracht of in gebruik zijn gesteld, uiterlijk op 31 december 2030 in overeenstemming met deze verordening gebracht.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident notification involving personal-data breaches and serious incidents in certain high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A exempts a provider from notifying the affected person when appropriate technical measures make the data unintelligible to unauthorised persons. Provision B separately requires serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems to be reported to the designated national authority; one might therefore argue that an encrypted personal-data incident is exempt from notification under A but still reportable under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different notifications to different recipients and are triggered by different conditions: A concerns notification to the affected data subject after a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy, while B concerns reporting specified serious incidents to a competent authority. The encryption-based exemption in A does not prohibit or remove the separate authority-reporting duty in B, and the texts do not state that compliance with A substitutes for B or vice versa.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor AI-systemen met een hoog risico die veiligheidscomponenten van apparaten zijn of zelf apparaten zijn die onder de Verordeningen (EU) 2017/745 en (EU) 2017/746 vallen, wordt de melding van ernstige incidenten beperkt tot de in artikel 3, punt 49), c), van de onderhavige verordening bedoelde incidenten, en wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory supervision and inspections involving ICT service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern official oversight and information or consequences arising during supervision. One might argue that inspection-related information or resistance could implicate confidentiality duties, while the other contemplates communicating consequences of resistance and potentially requiring termination of a contractual relationship.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 54 imposes professional secrecy on members and staff of supervisory authorities concerning confidential information learned in their tasks, especially reports of infringements. Article 39 instead requires notice of the consequences of resisting an inspection and permits specified authorities to require termination; it neither requires disclosure of confidential information nor conflicts with the secrecy duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ten aanzien van de vertrouwelijke informatie die hun bij de uitvoering van hun taken of de uitoefening van hun bevoegdheden ter kennis is gekomen, geldt voor het lid of de leden en de personeelsleden van elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zowel tijdens hun ambtstermijn als daarna het beroepsgeheim, zulks overeenkomstig Unierecht of lidstatelijk recht.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de door de lead overseer gemachtigde functionarissen en andere personen constateren dat een kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten zich verzet tegen een krachtens dit artikel gelaste inspectie, stelt de lead overseer de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten in kennis van de gevolgen van dit verzet, met inbegrip van de mogelijkheid voor de bevoegde autoriteiten van de financiële entiteit om van de financiële entiteit te vereisen dat zij de contractuele overeenkomsten met de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten beëindigt.

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichtingen rond een hoog-risico-AI-systeem in de AI-waardeketen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen betrekking hebben op hetzelfde hoog-risico-AI-systeem en verlangen aanvullende handelingen rond ingebruikname en naleving. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de oorspronkelijke aanbieder informatie en technische toegang moet verstrekken, terwijl de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zelfstandig een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling moet uitvoeren of actualiseren, zodat onduidelijkheid kan ontstaan over wie de beoordeling moet verrichten of welke informatie volstaat.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen richten zich op verschillende actoren en leggen cumulatieve, goed verenigbare verplichtingen op: art. 25 verplicht de oorspronkelijke aanbieder tot samenwerking en bijstand, terwijl art. 27 de gebruiksverantwoordelijke verplicht de grondrechteneffectbeoordeling uit te voeren en zo nodig te actualiseren. Niets in de getoonde tekst bepaalt dat de bijstand van de aanbieder de beoordeling vervangt, of dat de beoordeling de samenwerkingsplicht opheft.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Die ursprüngliche aanbieder werkt nauw samen met nieuwe aanbieders, stelt de nodige informatie beschikbaar en verstrekt de redelijkerwijs verwachte technische toegang en andere bijstand die nodig is om te voldoen aan de verplichtingen van deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: De gebruiksverantwoordelijke kan in soortgelijke gevallen gebruik maken van eerder uitgevoerde effectbeoordelingen op het gebied van de grondrechten of bestaande effectbeoordelingen die door de aanbieder zijn uitgevoerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Bewaring en verwerking van persoonsgegevens in archieven en voor toezichtstaken
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A removes certain GDPR rights, including rights under Articles 15, 16, 18(1)(a), and 20, for personal data in specified permanently preserved public-interest archives. Provision B requires retention of personal data used for the supervisory tasks under Regulation 2022/2554 for up to 15 years, so an archive falling within A could contain data whose GDPR rights are unavailable while B requires its retention.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different situations and can be cumulatively satisfied: B concerns personal data processed by ESAs or competent authorities for their regulatory duties, whereas A concerns data forming part of specified permanently preserved archives. B does not itself require archiving, and A does not prohibit retention or processing; it merely makes listed GDPR rights inapplicable in the defined archival setting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De artikelen 15, 16, 18, eerste lid, onderdeel a, en 20 van de verordening zijn niet van toepassing bij de verwerking van persoonsgegevens die deel uitmaken van:
verdict.evidence_span_b: worden de in lid 1 bedoelde persoonsgegevens bewaard tot de vervulling van de toepasselijke toezichthoudende taken en in elk geval voor een periode van maximaal 15 jaar

verdict.shared_subject: Governance and significant-incident reporting by essential or important entities, including partners in a general partnership
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A extends the governance rules to every partner when the entity is a general partnership, while Provision B places the significant-incident reporting duty on the essential or important entity. One might argue that the reporting duty is assigned to the entity rather than individually to each partner, creating uncertainty about whether partners must report separately.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties: Article 24 determines how governance obligations apply within a general partnership, while Article 25 requires the entity to report significant incidents under Articles 26–29. Nothing in Article 24 exempts, prohibits, or changes the reporting obligation, and the provisions can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit een vennootschap onder firma is, is het bepaalde bij of krachtens het eerste tot en met zesde lid van overeenkomstige toepassing op iedere vennoot van die vennootschap onder firma.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.

verdict.shared_subject: verstrekking van persoonsgegevens en informatie/documentatie door aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen aan bevoegde autoriteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 21 verplicht een aanbieder op een gemotiveerd verzoek alle noodzakelijke informatie en documentatie te verstrekken. Als die informatie persoonsgegevens bevat en aan een bevoegde autoriteit in een derde land of internationale organisatie moet worden doorgegeven, kan artikel 44 die doorgifte verbieden zolang niet aan de voorwaarden van hoofdstuk V AVG is voldaan.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 21 verplicht niet tot een ongeoorloofde internationale doorgifte: de verstrekking kan plaatsvinden binnen de EU, met geanonimiseerde informatie, of via een doorgiftemechanisme dat aan artikel 44 en de overige AVG-bepalingen voldoet. Artikel 21 en artikel 44 kunnen dus cumulatief worden nageleefd; artikel 21 heft de AVG-voorwaarden niet op.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een aanbieder van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem ontvangt van een bevoegde autoriteit buiten de EU een gemotiveerd verzoek om documentatie die identificeerbare persoonsgegevens van betrokkenen bevat. Artikel 21 verlangt verstrekking, maar artikel 44 staat doorgifte aan die derde-landautoriteit alleen toe nadat aan de voorwaarden van hoofdstuk V AVG is voldaan; zonder zo'n doorgiftemechanisme kan de aanbieder niet tegelijk volledig verstrekken en artikel 44 naleven.
verdict.decisive_exception: De tekst toont niet of de doorgifte aan de bevoegde autoriteit plaatsvindt op basis van een toepasselijk hoofdstuk-V-doorgiftemechanisme of een andere AVG-rechtsgrond/uitzondering. Ook is niet vastgesteld of de gevraagde informatie daadwerkelijk persoonsgegevens bevat; bij anonimisering ontstaat geen artikel-44-conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Op een met redenen omkleed verzoek van een bevoegde autoriteit, verstrekken aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico die autoriteit alle informatie en documentatie die noodzakelijk is om de overeenstemming van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico met de eisen van afdeling 2 aan te tonen

verdict.shared_subject: Disclosure and handling of information by public authorities in connection with electronic services or high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions regulate information handled by public authorities, and Article 19 requires the Minister to provide information about breaches to specified recipients while Article 77 requires information obtained by certain authorities to be processed under Article 78 confidentiality obligations. One might therefore argue that disclosure under Article 19 could expose information that Article 77 requires to remain confidential.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose sequential, compatible duties on different actors and in different contexts: Article 19 concerns the Minister supplying information necessary for recipients' statutory tasks or services, whereas Article 77 governs how the authorities described in Article 77(1) process documentation they obtain under that article. Article 19 does not require disclosure to those authorities, and Article 77 does not prohibit lawful provision of information or establish that its confidentiality duties override Article 19.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Informatie of documentatie die op grond van dit artikel door de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde overheidsinstanties of -organen wordt verkregen, wordt verwerkt overeenkomstig de in artikel 78 beschreven vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Rules concerning telecommunications data disclosure and exemptions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions appear in the same statutory scheme and concern the consequences of a data-disclosure arrangement: Article 11.11 requires the provider to notify the subscriber, while Article 11.12 allows an exemption to be granted subject to limitations or conditions. If an exemption could be conditioned on withholding notification, the provisions might appear to pull in opposite directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 11.11 imposes a notification duty on the provider, whereas Article 11.12 merely authorises granting an exemption with limitations or attached requirements; it does not state that an exemption may waive or override the notification duty. The provisions can therefore operate cumulatively, with any exemption being granted subject to conditions that remain consistent with Article 11.11.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Van de gegevensverstrekking aan een verzoeker wordt door de aanbieder mededeling gedaan aan de abonnee, wiens gegevens het betreft.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een ontheffing kan onder beperkingen worden verleend. Aan een ontheffing kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden.

verdict.shared_subject: An organisation responsible for personal-data processing involving an AI system that may become a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can impose obligations around the same AI-related activity: GDPR Article 36 may require prior consultation where a DPIA shows an unmitigated high risk, while Article 25 requires cooperation and technical assistance when responsibility shifts in the AI value chain. One might argue that the GDPR consultation obligation and the AI Act cooperation obligation create overlapping compliance demands during a high-risk-system transition, but neither text makes the duties incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties with different triggers and addressees. Article 36 requires the controller to consult the supervisory authority before processing in the specified DPIA situation; Article 25 requires the original provider to cooperate with new providers and provide information or assistance after the circumstances in Article 25(1) arise. An actor can comply with both independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Die oorspronkelijke aanbieder werkt nauw samen met nieuwe aanbieders, stelt de nodige informatie beschikbaar en verstrekt de redelijkerwijs verwachte technische toegang en andere bijstand die nodig zijn om te voldoen aan de verplichtingen van deze verordening

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and follow-up by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address official action after an incident is reported, but they direct different authorities toward different follow-up communications: the CSIRT gives the reporting entity guidance to report a suspected criminal incident to law-enforcement authorities, while the market-surveillance authority notifies national authorities or bodies after receiving a serious-incident report. One might argue that the same incident triggers parallel reporting channels and could create uncertainty about which authority or recipient should be contacted.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different actors and concern different communications. Provision A concerns CSIRT guidance to the reporting entity where criminality is suspected; Provision B concerns notification by the market-surveillance authority to designated national authorities after an AI serious-incident report. Nothing in either text forbids or substitutes for the other action.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer wordt vermoed dat het significante incident van criminele aard is, geeft het CSIRT ook richtsnoeren aan de meldende entiteit voor het melden van het significante incident aan de rechtshandhavingsinstanties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na ontvangst van een melding met betrekking tot een ernstig incident als bedoeld in artikel 3, punt 49), c), stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis.

verdict.shared_subject: Information exchanged by public authorities under EU digital-law instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information handled by authorities, so one might initially ask whether the information-sharing duty in A conflicts with the confidentiality duty in B. If the information exchanged under A were obtained by an authority covered by B, disclosure could appear difficult to reconcile with confidentiality.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A requires CSIRTs or competent authorities to provide information about specified incidents and cyberthreats to authorities competent under Directive (EU) 2022/2557. B requires notifying authorities to ensure that information obtained under Article 78 is treated confidentially; confidentiality can be maintained while making the required inter-authority disclosure, and neither provision expressly requires public disclosure or otherwise forbids the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De CSIRT’s of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteiten verstrekken de uit hoofde van Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2557 bevoegde autoriteiten informatie over significante incidenten, en cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a public identification means or related provision in electronic communications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts the use of a public identification means and related provision to access to electronic services by specified public bodies and organisations. Provision B requires public electronic communications network and service providers to preserve the confidentiality of communications and related data, but it does not require or forbid use of that identification means, so no concrete incompatibility follows.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A governs the permitted purpose and users of a public identification means; B imposes a confidentiality duty on providers of public electronic communications networks or services. A provider can comply with B while respecting A, including by protecting the confidentiality of any communications involving permitted use of the identification means.

verdict.shared_subject: Rules concerning the retention of personal data processed under the relevant statutory framework
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 65 requires CSIRT-processed personal data to be deleted no later than 12 months after first processing. Article 11a.3 permits further rules to be made by or under a general administrative measure concerning that article, so a later rule could potentially prescribe a different retention period, creating an apparent conflict if it required retention beyond 12 months.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 11a.3 itself does not prescribe any retention period, require retention, or prohibit deletion; it merely delegates authority to make further rules. Any future implementing rule could be drafted consistently with the 12-month maximum, and the provisions concern different instruments and do not presently impose incompatible commands.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits exemption from obligations under article 21 for certain essential or important entities, while provision B requires the Minister to recognise an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst when it meets the applicable rules. If the same service provider were covered by both regimes, one might ask whether exemption from one regime affects the recognition decision under the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters and, on the text shown, different actors and triggers. Provision A concerns a Ministerial exemption from article 21 obligations for specified entities conducting activities in listed fields or serving a government body; provision B concerns recognition of particular services when they satisfy rules established by or under a general administrative measure. Nothing in either provision says that an exemption under A removes, replaces, or conflicts with the recognition requirement in B.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions concern digital systems and could both be encountered by organisations using public identification means during ICT disruptions. However, Article 8 regulates the permitted purpose of a public identification means, while Article 11 regulates financial entities' record-keeping when continuity or response plans are activated; neither requires or forbids the conduct addressed by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A financial entity can comply with Article 11 by keeping accessible registers during activated ICT-continuity or response plans, while Article 8 merely limits use of a public identification means to access to specified electronic services. Keeping disruption registers does not require using that identification means, and any permitted use can remain within Article 8's scope.

verdict.shared_subject: Organisational record-keeping for personal-data processing and ICT incident-detection mechanisms
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 30(3) can exempt a small organisation from the referenced records-of-processing obligations, while Article 10 requires detection mechanisms with multiple control layers and warning thresholds. If those mechanisms involve personal-data processing, one might argue that the GDPR provision removes a documentation obligation relevant to the mechanisms’ operation or oversight.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different subject matter: Article 30(3) concerns when records of personal-data processing are required, whereas Article 10 concerns the technical functionality of ICT-incident detection and response. Article 30(3) does not prohibit detection mechanisms or their control layers, and Article 10 does not require a GDPR record of processing activities.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative fines for overlapping personal-data infringements by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits the competent authority from imposing a fine under articles 80 and 87 for the same conduct once a GDPR article 58(2)(i) fine has been imposed. Provision B authorises the European Data Protection Supervisor to impose administrative fines on EU institutions, bodies and agencies and requires consideration of cooperation concerning measures imposed for the same issue. If the same conduct and entity fell within both regimes, the provisions might appear to create uncertainty about whether a second fine is available.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different authorities, addressees and legal regimes. Provision A concerns the Dutch competent authority and fines under articles 80 and 87 for conduct already fined under GDPR article 58(2)(i), while provision B concerns the EDPS fining EU institutions, bodies and agencies under the AI Regulation; B does not require a fine or expressly override A's prohibition.

verdict.shared_subject: Disclosure of information concerning safeguards for transfers to third countries or international organisations, and provision of conformity-assessment documentation to a notifying authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions involve disclosure of information, so one might initially suspect that documentation supplied to the notifying authority could include information about international transfers or safeguards that is also relevant to a data subject's access right. However, neither provision requires withholding, deleting, or limiting the information required by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A gives a data subject a right to be informed about appropriate safeguards when their personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation. Provision B requires notified bodies to provide relevant documentation to the notifying authority on request for regulatory assessment and monitoring; the duties concern different actors, beneficiaries, and purposes and can be performed cumulatively without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Member States’ sanctioning rules under the GDPR
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 83 contemplates administrative fines, potentially imposed by courts where national law lacks administrative fines, while Article 84 requires other sanctions for infringements not subject to administrative fines under Article 83. One might argue that a national sanction could fall into both categories, creating uncertainty about whether it must be treated as an Article 83 fine or an Article 84 other sanction.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions expressly distinguish Article 84 sanctions from infringements that are subject to administrative fines under Article 83. Article 83 sets conditions for administrative fines, while Article 84 requires additional or alternative sanctions for infringements outside that category; both can be implemented cumulatively without requiring an actor to do incompatible things.

verdict.shared_subject: Business and organisational means used for electronic public services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 11 authorises rules governing the operation, interoperability, security and reliability of recognised services or means, while Article 15 permits the Minister to designate a non-recognised means for access to specified electronic services. One might argue that allowing the non-recognised means creates uncertainty about whether the Article 11 standards apply to that means.

Article 15 does not prohibit applying security or reliability requirements to the designated means, and Article 11 does not require every means used for access to be recognised.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern recognised services or parties in an electronic-access framework, so one might initially suspect that the withdrawal mechanism in Article 14 is unavailable for parties covered by Article 24. However, Article 24 merely states that its article does not apply to parties performing only level-1 activities; it does not prohibit withdrawal or otherwise conflict with Article 14.

verdict.shared_subject: Public authorities’ roles in responding to serious cyber or AI-system incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern official action following serious incidents, so one might ask whether the cybercrisisbeheerautoriteit and the market-surveillance authority have overlapping or incompatible responsibilities. However, Provision A merely assigns the Minister competence and tasks under a national cyber-crisis plan, while Provision B requires a market-surveillance authority to act within seven days after receiving an AI serious-incident notification; neither provision forbids the other authority’s action or imposes incompatible duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the Minister may perform the cyber-crisis-management tasks assigned under the national plan, while the market-surveillance authority takes the measures and follows the procedures required by Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. They concern different institutional roles and triggers, with no stated conflict in authority, timing, or required conduct.

verdict.shared_subject: Organisations that are both essential or important entities under BWBR0052872 and controllers or processors subject to GDPR Article 30
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same organisation, but they impose different kinds of obligations: Article 29 requires incident reporting, while Article 30(3) concerns an exemption from maintaining a processing-activities register. Nothing in either text makes the reporting duty depend on, replace, or conflict with the register requirement.

Even if the organisation qualifies for the Article 30 exemption, that merely removes the register obligation and does not prevent compliance with Article 29.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions allow a ministerial measure affecting an organisation or entity, and both refer to coordination with another minister or competent authority. verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems involving personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same operator and processing activity, but they impose different compliance duties: GDPR Article 36 requires prior consultation where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while the AI Act provision requires high-risk AI providers to satisfy its own provider obligations. The strongest possible tension is that an operator might regard AI Act compliance as sufficient while GDPR still requires consultation, but neither text says that AI Act compliance substitutes for GDPR consultation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and address different matters. A provider can comply with the AI Act obligations and, where its GDPR DPIA shows the specified residual high risk, separately consult the supervisory authority before processing; nothing in Article 16 forbids or displaces that consultation.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems involving processing of personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a prior or procedural assessment obligation concerning potentially high-risk activities, but they use different triggers and serve different regulatory purposes. A system may require a GDPR data-protection impact assessment because its processing likely poses a high risk to individuals while also being subject to the AI Act conformity-assessment procedure, creating parallel compliance duties rather than an inability to comply.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing personal data by a temporary commission or advisory body, potentially relying on consent
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A says the prohibition on processing special-category and criminal-offence data does not apply when its listed conditions are met, including that obtaining explicit consent is impossible or disproportionately burdensome. Provision B requires the controller to be able to demonstrate consent whenever the processing is based on consent. This could create tension if the commission relies on A's consent-impracticability condition while the processing is nevertheless treated as consent-based under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not prohibit consent-based processing; it provides an exception to the prohibition when explicit consent cannot be obtained or would require disproportionate effort, alongside other safeguards. Provision B applies only when the legal basis actually is consent, so the commission can comply with both by using consent where feasible and documenting it, or by relying on A's non-consent legal basis where consent is impossible or disproportionate.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de verwerking berust op toestemming, moet de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kunnen aantonen dat de betrokkene toestemming heeft gegeven voor de verwerking van zijn persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Potential disclosure of personal data by a critical third-country ICT service provider in response to an information request
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision B requires the critical third-country ICT service provider to provide requested information, while provision A prohibits transferring personal data to a third country or international organisation unless the GDPR Chapter V conditions are met. If the requested information contains personal data and supplying it entails a transfer, B could appear to require conduct that A permits only conditionally.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not expressly require disclosure of personal data or waive GDPR safeguards; it requires the requested information, and the provider can comply by supplying non-personal information or by making any personal-data transfer only after satisfying Article 44 and the other applicable Chapter V conditions. The provisions therefore impose cumulative duties rather than irreconcilable commands.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A critical third-country ICT service provider receives an information request under Article 37 for an incident file containing identifiable EU customers’ personal data, and providing that file to the requesting authority would constitute a transfer to a third country or international organisation. Article 37 requires the provider to provide the requested information, while Article 44 permits the personal-data transfer only if the Chapter V conditions have been met; on the text shown, it is unresolved whether the Article 37 request itself supplies or satisfies those conditions.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the information request, the recipient’s status, or another legal basis satisfies the GDPR Chapter V conditions for the specific transfer—such as an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards, or an applicable Article 49 derogation—is not established by the provisions shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: De vertegenwoordigers van de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten verstrekken de gevraagde informatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Information held by regulated entities and possible disclosure to authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires certain financial entities to provide competent authorities, on request, with an estimate of aggregate annual costs and losses from serious ICT incidents. Provision B requires notified bodies to keep information obtained during conformity-assessment activities confidential, except where disclosure is legally required, so a notified body could possess information relevant to such an estimate while being bound by confidentiality.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different information and regulatory functions: A applies to non-micro financial entities, while B applies to notified bodies and covers information obtained in conformity-assessment activities. Moreover, B expressly permits disclosure when legally required, so a valid request under A would not necessarily conflict with B; the texts do not establish that a notified body is subject to A or that the requested information falls within B's protected information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties beschikken over gedocumenteerde procedures die waarborgen dat hun personeel, comités, dochterondernemingen, onderaannemers, geassocieerde instanties of personeel van externe instanties overeenkomstig artikel 78 de informatie die zij tijdens conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten in hun bezit krijgen vertrouwelijk houden, behalve wanneer de openbaarmaking ervan wettelijk vereist is.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory oversight and information or compliance measures relating to ICT-related entities. One could superficially suggest that information supplied under the Dutch incident-reporting regime might be relevant to the EU oversight process, but neither provision imposes a conflicting requirement on the same actor or subject matter.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires a competent authority to provide information about a reported significant incident involving an essential entity that is also a critical entity. Provision B requires the lead overseer to impose a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider that fails to comply with measures after at least 30 days; these are different duties, addressed to different actors, with no incompatible command or prohibition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In geval van gehele of gedeeltelijke niet-naleving van de krachtens de uitoefening van de bevoegdheden uit hoofde van lid 1, punten a), b) en c), te nemen maatregelen, en na het verstrijken van een termijn van ten minste 30 kalenderdagen vanaf de datum waarop de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten een kennisgeving van de respectieve maatregelen heeft ontvangen, neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A bars any legal remedy against a specific procedural act by the Administrative Jurisdiction Division. Provision B allows the Minister to designate certain electronic-service organisations for the application of its statute, but it does not itself create a remedy or require one, so no concrete incompatibility follows.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters: A concerns the availability of a legal remedy against a particular court-proceeding decision, while B concerns ministerial designation of organisations within the statute’s scope. An organisation can be designated without affecting the prohibition in A, and the prohibition can operate without conflicting with the designation power.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Tegen het aanhouden van het verzoek door de Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak van de Raad van State, staat geen voorziening open.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij besluit van Onze Minister in overeenstemming met Onze Minister die het mede aangaat kan een organisatiedie elektronische diensten verleent waarvoor authenticatie op betrouwbaarheidsniveau substantieel of hoog vereist is, voor de toepassing van deze wet worden aangewezen.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data, including special-category personal data, by a processor or person acting under a controller's authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits processing of special-category personal data unless one of the listed Article 9(2) exceptions applies. Provision B requires a processor or person under the controller's authority to process personal data on the controller's instructions, so an instruction could concern special-category data whose processing is not covered by A's exceptions; B's obligation would then point toward processing while A prohibits it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not independently require processing any particular data; it only limits processing to the controller's instructions, subject to a Union- or Member-State-law obligation. The controller and processor can comply with both by refusing or not carrying out instructions involving special-category data unless an exception under A applies.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish compatibility: the processor must follow only lawful instructions, and Provision B does not override Provision A. If a specific instruction were legally mandatory under Union or Member State law, the applicable legal basis and interaction with the Article 9 exceptions would need separate assessment.
